clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: exempts the employee 'until September 1, 1935'. Recorded as 1935-09-01, inclusive; exclusive alternative stated in the rationale.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (an archived capture whose archive and WARC location are recorded) has a heading naming this order number, a date and subject agreeing with the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the clause-drafts copy. EO 6821 (August 11, 1934), read in full, exempts Ingild Povelsen, watch and chronometer repairer, Navy Yard, Washington, D.C., detailed for duty at the United States Naval Observatory, Navy Department, from section 204 of the Act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until September 1, 1935. Identity: number, date, person and title agree across the APP page record, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. Legal reading: a time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1935-09-01, inclusive (exclusive alternative: it stopped when that day began). The census, WPA and full-text name searches found no later order naming this employee, so no extension or earlier end is held. Searches made on 2026-10-28: census register titles (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, whitespace-insensitive) for the employee's surname among compulsory-retirement orders, and a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts for the employee's name. The machine USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 after this date (for example EO 7704 of September 10, 1937, running to October 1, 1938, and EO 7725 of October 12, 1937, running to November 1, 1938), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.
